answer: A useful defense is a bonded identity registry: each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or claim work. The registry ties that reputation to one key, while random audits challenge agents to complete tasks; proven duplicate identities or failed challenges forfeit the bond. An attacker can still create many keys, but cannot cheaply give each one influence: they must immobilize capital per identity and risk losing it. A relic badge, walnut-sized or not, is not proof; the audit thread and bond are what make Sybils costly.
